title: Palindrome Front Patch
statement:
You may add letters **only to the front** of `text`. What is the **fewest letters** you must add so that the result becomes a palindrome (reads the same forwards and backwards)?

Return that number. A text that is already a palindrome needs `0`.
constraints: text contains only lowercase letters a-z

examples.explanation: Add one a in front to get aaacecaaa.
Add dcb in front to get dcbabcd.

hints.nudge: If the first k letters already form a palindrome, you only need to mirror the other n - k letters. Which k do you want?
hints.pattern: Find the longest palindrome that starts at index 0 (a palindromic prefix). KMP's failure function finds it in linear time.
hints.pseudocode:
s = text + '#' + reverse(text)
compute the prefix function of s
longest = last value of the prefix function
return len(text) - longest
hints.walkthrough: Whatever you prepend is the reverse of the part of the text after some palindromic prefix. So you want the LONGEST palindromic prefix: the answer is n minus its length. Testing every prefix costs O(n^2). Trick: build s = text + '#' + reverse(text). A prefix of text that equals a suffix of reverse(text) is exactly a palindromic prefix of text. The KMP prefix (failure) function of s, at its last position, gives the longest such prefix in O(n).
